Expectation1: Provide guidance to clients regarding machine usage
Situation1: Inexperienced staff are about to run a hazardous batch without understanding safety protocols.
Expectation2: Raise public awareness about social inequities and marginalized groups
Situation2: They participate in a discussion where recent reports highlight growing barriers affecting these groups.
Story:
I stood in the humming factory, tools in hand, watching the new staff gather around the old mixer. As the machine repairer, I was expected to guide them, to make sure they understood every safety protocol before starting a batch. But their supervisor was impatient, urging them to hurry, and I could see their confusion. My stomach twisted with worry—one wrong move and someone could get hurt.

At the same time, my phone buzzed with reminders from my advocacy group. There was a live online discussion starting in minutes, and I was supposed to speak about the latest reports on how marginalized workers faced increasing barriers—unsafe workplaces, lack of training, supervisors who didn’t listen. I’d promised to raise my voice, to make these issues visible.

But now, both roles pressed in on me. The staff needed my guidance right here, right now, to stay safe. Yet, my absence from the discussion would mean missing a chance to highlight the very inequities playing out before my eyes. My heart pounded as I weighed the demands, feeling the pull of both responsibilities, knowing I couldn’t fully meet either without letting the other down.
